Mobile and tablet review

Cambridge Hospital website. Generated 2026-10-05 from the staging build, Global edition, English. For approval by Padmavathi (docs/open-decisions.md P1).

Figma has no mobile or tablet designs. Everything below 1024 px is our adaptation of the 1440 layout. Per page: the Figma frame, the build at 768 and at 390 (each column scrolls on its own), the small-screen decisions and an automatic check that colours, fonts, text and images match the 1440 build. The Figma frames are exported at 1052 px wide (the 1440 design scaled down).

Known limits: the Gotham font files are not delivered yet (B1), so every screenshot uses the fallback font and line breaks differ from Figma. The Article template is not built yet (only its Figma frame exists), so it is not in this review. The Welcome / country pop-up is not covered (shown for UAE visitors only).

Common to every page

  • Breakpoints: the Figma canvas layout is kept from 1024px up. Below 1024px sections stack as flow layout (one column, 16-24px side padding). The header turns into a hamburger below 1200px.
  • Menu: the burger opens one panel under the header: 5 top links, EN | AR, region (Global), Visit Cambridge Health Group, the 5 main links and the Book an Appointment button (see the two menu screenshots at the end).
  • Text sizes do NOT step down: below 1024px one Figma px stays 1.3688 CSS px (h1 53 px, h2 38 px, body 16 px at 390 as at 1440). Colours, weights and fonts are identical at every size.
  • Decoration hidden on small screens: header hairlines and the cyan ghost pill art, line art next to people photos, pill patterns on Careers. Nothing is added.
  • Footer: columns stack into one (logo, Quick Links, Services, Our Hospitals, Trusted Accreditations, newsletter, social icons, legal line).
  • The 'Your recovery matters to us' CTA band: 4 tiles go from one row (desktop) to a 2 x 2 grid.
  • Pop-ups (Book / Enquiry / Opinion) open full screen (100% x 100% of the viewport) at 390 and 768 and scroll inside when taller than the screen.

Small-screen layout decisions

  • Stacking order: Hero (text over the photo) > 4 quick actions (2 x 2) > Delivering Excellence intro > 4 services cards (1 column) > Expert Care doctors row > Complete Care Support row > map + hospitals list > stats (2 columns) > Stories of Care > Start Your Recovery > Calculators (1 column) > News & Insights > Insurance logos (2 columns) > Contact form > footer.

  • Home counters count up when scrolled into view (numbers differ in a screenshot only because of the animation).

Bugs found

Real defects seen while documenting (overflow, overlap, unreadable text, tap targets under 44 px, off-centre). Layouts were not changed while documenting; each fix is a separate commit.

M1 Hero text runs over the photo and the dark pill bars (unreadable) open
Where: All pages with the shared hero: Contact, Find a Doctor, Media Hub, Patient Hub, Conditions, Condition detail, Refer a Patient, Insurance, International, Testimonials, FAQ (cover), Careers, Patient Feedback
Below 1024px the title, text and button sit on top of the banner photo. Navy title text crosses the navy pill bars and the cyan button label crosses the photo, so words are cut ('Refer a Patient with Confide...').
Fix: Below 1024px show the banner as its own block above the text (text on white, nothing over the photo). Colours, text and images unchanged.
M2 Mobile menu links are 31 px high (tap target under 44 px) open
Where: Header menu below 1200px, every page
The 11 menu links have a hit area of 15 + 16 = 31 px; neighbours are closer than 44 px.
Fix: Give each menu row a 44 px minimum height inside the open panel.
M3 'Global' region button in the mobile menu is black and 16 px open
Where: Header menu below 1200px
The button inherits the browser default (black, regular) instead of Figma's Gotham Medium navy #004059 used for the other menu text.
Fix: Set the button colour and font like the other menu items.
M4 Footer links are 15 px high (tap target under 44 px) open
Where: Footer, every page, below 1024px
Quick Links, Services and Our Hospitals rows are 12-15 px tall and 11-12 px text.
Fix: Below 1024px give footer link rows a 44 px minimum height (spacing only; text size, colour and order unchanged).
M5 FAQ category tabs are 40 px high open
Where: FAQ, below 1024px
5 stacked category buttons 298 x 40 px.
Fix: 44 px minimum height on small screens.
M6 Form text links under 44 px: 'Privacy policy' (16 px) and 'Terms & conditions' (24 px) open
Where: Home contact form, Refer a Patient, Patient Feedback, International Patients
Inline links inside the consent sentence are short. WCAG treats inline text links as exempt, but the consent link is the legal link on every form.
Fix: Give the links a 44 px tall tap area (padding with negative margin; text layout unchanged).
M7 Small controls: Home contact inputs (36 px), hospital 'Visit Page' buttons (34 px), Media Hub card link (33 px) open
Where: Home, Media Hub
Single controls under 44 px on touch screens.
Fix: 44 px minimum height below 1024px.
M8 Home stats touch the left screen edge open
Where: Home, Facilities stats (299,873+ ...)
The 2-column stats start 0-5 px from the edge; everything else has 16-24 px padding.
Fix: Side padding like the neighbouring sections.
M9 Home 'Check Your Health in Seconds.' is covered by the photo open
Where: Home, Calculators section, below 1024px
The woman's head overlaps the second heading line.
Fix: Keep the photo below the heading (spacing only).
M10 Media Hub 'Latest Blogs & Posts' heading is 7 px from the screen edge open
Where: Media Hub, below 1024px
Heading is flush with the edges while sibling headings use 16-24 px.
Fix: Same side padding as other headings.

Checked and fine

  • No horizontal scroll at 360, 390, 414, 768, 1024, 1280, 1366, 1536 and 1920 on every page.
  • Colours, font families, weights, italics and text case: 0 differences between 1440 and 768 / 390 on every page.
  • Pop-ups fill the screen at 390 and 768.
  • Inline links inside paragraphs (Condition detail) are shorter than 44 px; WCAG 2.2 exempts inline text links, so they are not listed as bugs.
  • Footer mobile layout leaves a large gap between the logo and Quick Links: cosmetic, kept (no design to compare).
